message.content:
### Quick answer - **`docker start `** starts an *existing container*, not the Docker engine itself. - To start the Docker **service/daemon** on Windows you need to start the **Docker Desktop** application (or the underlying Windows service). Below are the ways to do it: | Goal | How to do it | |------|--------------| | **Start Docker Desktop (GUI)** | Double‑click the Docker Desktop icon from the Start menu or taskbar. | | **Start the Docker Windows service (CLI)** | Run PowerShell as Administrator and execute:
`Start-Service Docker`
or
`sc start Docker` | | **Check status of Docker service** | `Get-Service Docker` (PowerShell) or `sc query Docker` (CMD) | | **Stop Docker service** | `Stop-Service Docker` or `sc stop Docker` | --- ### Why `docker start` alone won’t work `docker start` is a client command that talks to the Docker daemon. If the daemon isn’t running, the command will fail with something like: ``` Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock. Is the docker daemon running? ``` So you first need to ensure the Docker daemon/service is up. --- ### Step‑by‑step guide #### 1. Verify Docker Desktop is installed ```powershell Get-Command docker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue ``` If nothing returns, install Docker Desktop from https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop. #### 2. Start Docker Desktop (recommended) ```powershell & "$env:ProgramFiles\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe" ``` This launches the GUI; once the whale icon turns blue, Docker is ready. #### 3. Start the Docker service directly (no GUI) Open PowerShell **as Administrator** and run: ```powershell Start-Service Docker ``` You’ll see output like: ``` Status Name DisplayName ------ ---- ----------- Running Docker Docker Desktop Service ``` If you prefer CMD: ```cmd sc start Docker ``` #### 4. Confirm Docker is running ```powershell docker version ``` You should see client and server versions printed. --- ### Common pitfalls & troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | “Cannot connect to the Docker daemon” | Make sure the Docker service is running (`Start-Service Docker`). | | Docker Desktop fails to start | Restart your computer, then launch Docker Desktop again. | | Docker Desktop shows “Docker Desktop is starting…” forever | Check Windows Event Viewer → Applications and Services Logs → Docker Desktop. Often a corrupted config file causes this; deleting `%APPDATA%\Docker` may help. | | You’re on Windows Server (not Desktop) | Use the Docker Engine service (`com.docker.service`) instead of Docker Desktop. | --- ### Automating startup (optional) If you want Docker to start automatically when you log in: ```powershell Set-Service Docker -StartupType Automatic ``` Now the Docker service will start at boot, and you can still launch Docker Desktop manually if you need the GUI. --- ### TL;DR - **`docker start `** → starts a container. - **To start Docker itself**: run PowerShell as Admin → `Start-Service Docker` (or `sc start Docker`). - Once the service is running, you can start containers with `docker start `.
